# PT3-02 — Native Apple II Mockingboard playback validation

**Status:** design only; implementation and native-playback results pending  
**Target:** Apple II+/IIe, NMOS 6502, standard Mockingboard (physical slot 4), 50 Hz VIA Timer 1  
**Input:** PT3 modules generated by the PSID → native register capture → MIDI → Spectrumizer pipeline of [PR #271](https://github.com/RetroAppleJS/RetroAppleJS.github.io/pull/271)  
**Reference player:** Vince (Deater) Weaver's [`pt3_lib` v0.5](https://github.com/deater/dos33fsprogs/tree/master/music/pt3_lib), 6502/ca65

## 1. Decision and scope

PT3-02 proves that **real 6502 code** decodes the generated PT3 and writes real VIA port transactions to the existing Mockingboard emulator, while the Apple II foreground continues executing. The host must not decode PT3 or inject AY registers. Reuse the already implemented 6522 Timer 1, CPU IRQ line, AY bus, audio renderer, Mockingboard history and WAV recording.

**In scope:** three AY voices; simultaneous mirrored output on AY0 and AY1; default 50 Hz IRQ playback; play, loop, stop; source-clock pitch correction; register trace and timing; HGR page 1 contention; 10 fps and VBLANK-speed emulator modes; baseline on II+/IIe.

**Out of scope:** six independent AY voices, new AY synthesizers, MIDI/transcoder improvements, arbitrary IRQ chaining, IIc/IIGS-specific ROM/Language Card workarounds, sideloading during active IRQ, DOS disk-I/O coexistence, packaging as a TSR resident across unrelated programs, native Mockingboard hardware verification. Those are future phases.

## 2. Evidence used for the design

- Weaver's `README.pt3_lib`: approximately 3 KB RAM **plus song**, about 10–15% CPU at 50 Hz depending on song, 26 zero-page locations, page-aligned PT3 data, original 1.77 MHz AY module clock versus ~1 MHz Mockingboard clock.
- `pt3_lib_mockingboard_setup.s`: software IRQ vector at `$03FE/$03FF`, VIA0 Timer 1 continuous IRQ, original `$4FE7` latch, `CLI` in `pt3_test.s`.
- `pt3_lib_irq_handler.s`: acknowledges VIA0 T1 by reading `$C404`; PT3 frame decode; writes R0–R13 to *both* AY chips, omitting R13 when the decoded value equals `$FF` (to avoid unwanted envelope retriggers).
- `pt3_lib/zp.inc`: variables and register image occupy `$60–$7F` (reserve this complete block initially).
- RetroAppleJS `res/EMU_CARD_mockingboard.js`: two cycle-driven 6522s with `N+2` Timer 1 period, real IRQ-source assertion, VIA-to-AY transactions, `getHistoryJSON()` and `getViaState()`; history stores four bytes per event and supports buffers up to 1024 KB.
- Existing `asm/AUDIO/AY_SCORE_TIMING_MB06A3.S` and `tools/AY_SCORE_MB06A3_VERIFY_core.js` demonstrate CPU-cycle/IRQ/HGR measurement and musical pitch verification.
- Weaver's `music/pt3_lib/LICENSE`: dual choice of **0BSD or GPL-2.0-only**. If code is vendored, preserve the upstream license/attribution and record the exact source commit.

## 3. Data flow

```text
PSID --[native jsSID register capture]--> MIDI --[Spectrumizer]--> PT3
                                                                  |
                                                                  v
                                             [6502 RAM, page-aligned PT3]
                                                                  |
        Apple II CPU  <--- IRQ --- VIA0 T1 (~50 Hz)                 |
             |                                                    |
             +----> 6502 PT3 decoder (Weaver pt3_lib) <-----------+
                          |
                          +---- 6522 VIA0 port A/B ---> AY0 (A/B/C)
                          |
                          +---- 6522 VIA1 port A/B ---> AY1 (mirror)
                          |
                          +---- RTI ---> foreground HGR/game loop

Passive debug only: CPU/IRQ trace + AY register history + WAV capture.
```

The player owns **only one** Mockingboard T1 interrupt source. Both AY chips are programmed, but VIA1 T1 is **not** a second music IRQ.

## 4. Memory map (initial implementation proposal)

| Address | Responsibility | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$0000–$00FF` | Zero page | Reserve `$60–$7F` for pt3_lib; avoid conflicts |
| `$03FE–$03FF` | ROM/Monitor soft IRQ vector | Save on entry; restore on exit |
| `$2000–$3FFF` | HGR page 1 | Foreground test owns it |
| `$4000–$5FFF` | HGR page 2 | Available for later graphics stress test |
| `$6000–$6FFF` | PT3 6502 code/state candidate | Linker asserts image <= 4096 bytes |
| `$7000–$7FFF` | Foreground code or test diagnostics | No player/song overlap |
| `$8000–$8FFF` | PT3 song candidate, aligned at `$8000` | Initially accept <= 4096 bytes |
| `$C400–$C40F` | Physical slot 4 / VIA0 | Timer 1 + left AY |
| `$C480–$C48F` | Physical slot 4 / VIA1 | Right AY |

**These are candidate placements, not verified linker results.** Reject oversize binaries/songs and overlapping segments; do not silently relocate into I/O or DOS RAM. This first layout is for a dedicated native playback test. DOS 3.3 and arbitrary applications may occupy other memory and zero-page regions, so installation in a shared runtime needs its own integration phase.

Physical Mockingboard **slot 4** is represented by legacy RetroAppleJS internal **SlotN 5** in existing MB-06 diagnostics. Do not confuse those identifiers in telemetry.

## 5. Boot/install/stop contract

1. Assemble original pt3_lib with `ca65`/`ld65` and a small explicit test wrapper; **do not replace the 6502 decoder with JavaScript**. Build pinned sources with a recorded upstream SHA.
2. Produce two loadable binaries (player and PT3), or a reproducible test disk; load before enabling music. Verify PT3 page alignment, bounds and checksum.
3. With `SEI`, save prior soft IRQ vector and any VIA state we intend to modify; verify the test owns the card and no competing IRQ timer player is active.
4. Initialize both AY chips, set `PT3_LOC`, initialize song state; configure VIA0 T1; install the handler; `CLI`.
5. Run an independent foreground loop: first NOP counter, then HGR page 1 writes. Do not pace music from video refresh or host audio callbacks.
6. On explicit stop or song completion: `SEI`, mask VIA0 T1 IRQ, acknowledge any pending own flag, mute AY0/AY1, restore the saved soft IRQ vector and owned VIA configuration where safe; `CLI` only if interrupts were enabled before installation.
7. Confirm no further AY music transactions or pending owned IRQ after stop. Do not attempt to reconstruct port output latches by blind writes, because they can trigger AY transactions.

Original pt3_lib does **not** generically chain a foreign IRQ handler; PT3-02 must require exclusive IRQ ownership. Future integration can use an explicit dispatcher/chain implementation after its semantics are proven.

For the initial test, compile slot 4 directly. Only after baseline success enable slot detection/patching and test that non-slot-4 configurations behave safely. The upstream readme explicitly warns that its fast patching can replace unrelated `$C4` bytes.

## 6. Timing contract

- Source: VIA0 Timer 1 free-run; hardware model gives period `T1_latch + 2` CPU cycles. The upstream `$4FE7` latch yields **20457 cycles** per tick.
- Emulator truth: read actual `clockHz` from Mockingboard history / CPU tick configuration. Do not assume exactly 1,000,000 CPU ticks per second. Under a 1,021,800 tick/s configuration, `$4FE7` corresponds to approximately **49.95 Hz**, sufficiently close for baseline.
- **Mode REF:** upstream unmodified timer latch and pitch-conversion settings, to establish compatibility.
- **Mode CAL:** after REF passes, use the calculated 50 Hz latch `round(clockHz / 50) - 2`, preserving correct 6522 `N+2` behavior. Keep both result series separate.
- IRQ measurements: T1 underflow timestamp, IRQ handler entry, acknowledgment, frame decoder entry/exit, last AY write, RTI, full ISR cycle cost, missed/late interrupt counts and 50 Hz period deviation.
- Never add a JS timer, synthesize periodic AY writes on the host, or scale the CPU clock to make timing appear correct.

On 1,021,800 ticks/s, one 50 Hz time slice is ~20,436 CPU cycles. At 10–15% overhead the *expected* average service burden is roughly **2,044–3,065 cycles per update**; these are contextual reference values, not measured PT3-02 results.

## 7. Tests, in dependency order

### PT3-02A — Native load and IRQ smoke test

- Build a tiny **original** PT3 fixture (known melody and stable pitches) with Spectrumizer; assert header/bounds/page alignment.
- Load 6502 player and PT3 into a standard Apple II+/IIe configuration, physical slot 4. Preserve original player IRQ semantics and compare REF timer behavior.
- Execute at least 250 ticks (5 seconds). Confirm successful initialization, 50 Hz timer behavior, uninterrupted returns to foreground, playback stop and no stuck IRQ.
- Control test: play an independently known-compatible PT3 module where redistribution rights allow (otherwise load locally without committing third-party music).

### PT3-02B — AY register equivalence and pitch

- Capture real `RetroAppleJS.MockingboardHistory` with `wrapped: false`; 256 KB is an initial practical buffer for multi-second mirrored two-chip traces.
- Compare AY0 and AY1 transactions against the 6502 player's frame register image (R0–R12 and R13 when not `$FF`). Exclude/reset-tag initialization writes and check their order separately.
- Verify no spurious R13 envelope retriggers; verify R7, tone period, volume, noise and envelope writes; verify mirrored AY1 data.
- For stable melody note windows, derive pitch from **the actual AY period**: `pitchHz = AY_clockHz / (16 * period)`. Compare against expected PT3/MIDI notes. Target within ±15 cents for non-modulated test notes (stricter target ±10 cents after tuning).
- Also capture a Mockingboard WAV. Listening is a qualitative check, not a substitute for register and frequency evidence.

### PT3-02C — CPU budget and HGR coexistence

- Execute 5-second NOP-loop baseline, then 5-second foreground HGR page-1 writes while the native player continues in IRQ context.
- Record mean/p95/max ISR cycles and percentage of all CPU cycles consumed by music. Record foreground progress (e.g. HGR writes/s) against a no-music run.
- Run both 10 fps presentation and VBLANK-speed modes for equal **emulated CPU-cycle durations**. Assert the same music register sequence, note pitches and IRQ count within defined clock/timer tolerances. Wall-clock render speed is **not** a musical clock.
- Check that the Mockingboard audio queue has no underruns/overruns that are wrongly attributed to the 6502 music decoder; report transport issues separately.

### PT3-02D — Converted corpus and teardown

- Test PT3 outputs from the three original MIDI fixtures and three repository SID songs of PR #271, generated during CI rather than redistributing third-party derivatives by default.
- Confirm all six PT3 files **load, run, complete or loop as configured, and produce nonempty AY output**.
- Do not claim SID-to-AY timbre or complete note preservation: PT3-01 has already shown substantial note-event reduction for real songs.
- Repeat start/stop, replay, repeated song load (only with IRQ stopped), normal end, loop and safe reset. Confirm IRQ vector and card ownership have been released.

## 8. Acceptance criteria

| Dimension | Mandatory acceptance | Performance target / diagnostic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native execution | Real 6502 code runs, VIA writes produce AY audio; no host PT3 playback | Independently compatible module also works |
| IRQ | Each expected T1 interrupt serviced exactly once; no stuck IRQ; handler returns | REF ~49.95 Hz; calibrated ~50 Hz |
| Register writes | AY0/AY1 match player register image, including R13 suppression | No unexpected AY resets |
| Pitch | Stable non-modulated test tones within ±15 cents | ±10 cents target |
| CPU | No IRQ update overruns its next timer deadline; foreground keeps progressing | Average music cost ~10–15%, investigate >20% |
| HGR | HGR writes continue during IRQ playback, without corruption of player/song RAM | Foreground throughput measured against no-music baseline |
| Display FPS | Identical emulated-time music sequence at 10 fps and VBLANK speed | Timing jitter and host audio metrics reported separately |
| Songs | 6/6 generated PT3 modules load and play or loop, with audible AY output | Qualitative listening ratings, song-by-song |
| Clean shutdown | No music IRQ or unexpected register traffic after stop/reset | Re-install succeeds without hard reset |
| Evidence | Machine-readable, reproducible telemetry and failed-gate details | WAV + AY history + cycle-budget report |

Any hard gate failing must report **REVIEW/FAIL**, not silently PASS based on software PT3 decoding. For long captures, `wrapped: true` is a failing condition for register-exact assertions; shorter windows or a larger buffer are required.

If the `pt3_lib` source is included locally, use an attributed folder under `asm/AUDIO/vendor/pt3_lib/` with its 0BSD license and pinned upstream commit; if fetched at build time, pin exact SHA and use a reliable cache. Choose one of these reproducible strategies when implementation begins.

**Outputs** (schema proposed): `PT3_02_native_results.json`, `PT3_02_irq_cycles.json`, `PT3_02_ay_history.json`, `PT3_02_mockingboard.wav`, linker map and assembled binary/disk image. Include version identifiers, song SHA-256, CPU clock, T1 latch, machine model, emulator backend, physical slot and software versions.

## 10. Risks, sequencing, and exit criterion

1. **Highest risk: PT3 subset compatibility.** Spectrumizer's decoder accepts the subset it emits; that does not prove Weaver's independent 6502 PT3 parser accepts it. Gate this in PT3-02A before investing in audio performance work.
2. **Clock correctness:** distinguish Atari/Spectrum PT3 tone tables, PT3 player frequency conversion and the actual Mockingboard AY clock; never apply correction twice. Prove pitch through real register values.
3. **IRQ/ROM safety:** `$03FE/$03FF` and `$45` behavior differs by Apple II model. Start with a fixed II+/IIe and single-owner harness. Do not generalize to IIc/IIGS prematurely.
4. **History pressure:** 13–14 AY registers multiplied by two chips and ~50 frames/s produce substantial write history; avoid wrapped captures.
5. **Memory conflicts:** linker map and test loader must check every segment, zero page and HGR reservation before executing.
6. **Software vs. hardware:** an emulator PASS does not establish performance on physical hardware. That needs a later test with a real Mockingboard.

**PT3-02 is complete only after independent native 6502 compatibility, clock/pitch, IRQ/HGR coexistence and clean-teardown gates pass.** PT3-01's successful software rendering alone cannot close it.
